sections.html:
The Lee County Register of Deeds answers at 919-718-4585. You will find it on South Horner Boulevard in Sanford, open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning to 5:00. Since January 1, 2017, the daily recording cutoff for every document has been 4:30.

The office exists to maintain, protect and provide access to every recorded transaction and the county's vital records. For a seller, the real estate side is what counts: it records properly notarized instruments, mostly concerning land in Lee County, and keeps the index that title examiners search.

Marriage licenses are by appointment only. If you need vital records for an estate sale, you can order certified copies online through the link on the county's Register of Deeds page.

Sanford's base price for a deed is $26.00 and covers 15 pages. Sheets after that run $4.00 each. Mortgages and deeds of trust start at $64.00 and cover 35 pages. The printed schedule cites G.S. 161-10, the statewide fee statute.

Lee County land record charges
ServicePrice
Deed and other non-mortgage instruments$26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per page
Loan documents (mortgage, deed of trust)$64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 for every added page
Cancellations of recordNo fee
Added instruments bundled in a filing$10.00 each
Out-of-standard document$25.00 plus the usual fees
Plat, new or revised$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy of a recorded instrument$5.00 to start, $2.00 per extra page
Copy without certification25 cents per page
Returned check$25.00

An additional subsequent instrument index reference is $25.00 each.

The schedule prints the state excise tax on real estate conveyances as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 up to $500. Under the statute the seller owes one dollar for each $500 of value, rounding any leftover amount up to a full unit, and pays at the register before recording.

The sheet also explains where the money goes. One half stays with the county, and the other half, less a 2 percent handling fee, goes to the state. That split is the county's bookkeeping and does not change what the seller owes.

Your closing attorney's settlement statement should show the excise line in the seller column, right beside recording. If the figure seems off for your contract price, phone the register.

Cancellations are free, which covers releasing an old deed of trust. A military discharge is also free to file, along with one certified copy of it.

Everything else follows the page-based fees. These are the items that usually come up when a Lee County house is sold:

  • The seller's deed to the buyer, priced by its length.
  • The buyer's deed of trust, if there is a loan, charged at the higher base.
  • A cancellation of the seller's old loan, recorded for no fee.
  • A plat, if a lot is being split, at $21.00 a sheet.

A cash sale has no new loan to record, so the register's bill is usually just the deed fee and the excise stamp, plus any copies you ask for.

sections.h2: Can I be alerted when something is recorded against my property?
sections.html:
Yes. The register offers a free property notification service. You register a name, and an email arrives whenever a document under that name is filed in the Lee County office. Sign-up runs through a state-wide notification website linked from the county page.

This suits owners who live away from a house, hold an inherited property, or rent a home out. A filing under your name that you did not expect is a red flag for fraud, and the email lets you call the office quickly.

You can also search deeds through the Sanford and Lee County deeds online portal that the county links. Use it to confirm that a deed from your closing has appeared and to read the book and page of earlier deeds.

The register issues certified copies of recorded instruments for $5.00 on the opening page plus $2.00 per page after it. A comparing copy for certification costs $5.00. These help when a lender or buyer's attorney asks for a stamped copy of an older deed, easement or plat.

Estate sales often need vital records too. Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records are $10.00 each in the schedule, and certified vital records can be ordered online through a link on the county page.

Other items on the schedule that can touch a sale:

  • A certificate for removal of graves, $12.00 for page one then $3.00 a page after that, which may come up when rural land with an old family plot is conveyed.
  • Right-of-way plans, $21.00 up front and $5.00 for every one after.
  • A UCC search for filings made before July 1, 2001, $38.00 per name plus $1.00 per copy.

Property tax is handled apart from the register. The Lee County Tax Office, 106 Hillcrest Drive in Sanford, lists and appraises real estate, personal property and registered motor vehicles, and it collects both current and delinquent taxes. It is open weekdays from eight to five.

Three direct lines cover the main needs:

  • Collections: 919-718-4662
  • Listings: 919-718-4661
  • Appraisals: 919-718-4660

The department's page offers a comparable sales tool called Comper, which sellers can use to see recorded sales near their address. On the bill itself, the due date is September 1 and no interest accrues before January 6. After that date 2 percent is added, then 3/4 percent a month from February 1.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Sanford office
sections.html:
A short trip to South Horner Boulevard goes better with the right papers in hand. Bring the signed and notarized deed, payment for the page fee and the seller's excise tax, and a clear idea of how many pages the deed runs. If a cancellation of an old loan is part of the closing, confirm with your lender who will send it, because the register records it without charge but cannot chase the lender for you.

Out-of-town sellers can skip the trip. The closing attorney or title company normally presents everything on your behalf, and the free notification service tells you once the filing under your name appears in the Lee County records.

Lee County has 70,258 residents, up 11.0 percent from 2020, and 28,511 housing units in a compact 255.06 square miles. A typical owned home is worth $240,200, and owners live in 67.3 percent of homes. The rest are rentals at a median $1,017. Builders took out 674 permits in 2025, so new homes are part of the supply, and a resale usually competes with them on price and move-in readiness.

Selling for cash to a direct buyer means no listing and no repair list, yet the paperwork still lands at this office. You sign the deed, the closing agent brings it in ahead of the 4:30 p.m. cutoff, and your excise tax is paid first.

Pull together your own deed, a payoff statement if a loan remains, and the latest tax bill before accepting an offer. Should a lien appear on the title, have the lender record its cancellation so the next owner gets a clear record.

On closing day the usual flow in Sanford is short. The attorney checks the deed, you sign before a notary, the excise stamp is paid, and the file reaches the register before 4:30. Afterward, ask for your lender's cancellation to be recorded, since that costs nothing, and keep the recorded copy with your closing papers.

faqs.q: What time does the Lee County Register of Deeds stop recording documents?
faqs.a: 4:30 p.m. every day. Staff are there until five on weekdays, but recording has ended half an hour sooner since January 1, 2017.

faqs.q: What will a Lee County deed cost at the register's counter?
faqs.a: $26.00 buys 15 pages, and every further page is $4.00. Mortgage paperwork is $64.00 for 35 pages. The excise stamp is extra.

faqs.q: Does Lee County charge to cancel a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. No. Recording a cancellation of an old loan is free, so it adds nothing to what you pay at closing.

faqs.q: Who is charged the transfer stamp on a Lee County deed?
faqs.a: The seller. The transferor settles it with the register before recording, at one dollar per $500 of price, with any remainder counted as another unit.

faqs.q: Is there a free alert for new filings under my name in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers a free property notification service that emails you when a document with your registered name is filed in the Lee County office.
